title: Finite-type points admit field representatives with etale self-relation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $\mathcal X$ an algebraic stack over $S$, and $x\in|\mathcal X|$ a finite-type point. Assume $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. There is a field $k$ and a representative $a:\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal X$ of $x$ which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], such that both projections of the algebraic space $\operatorname{Spec}k\times_{\mathcal X}\operatorname{Spec}k$ to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. No Noetherian or perfectness hypothesis is imposed on $S$ or $k$. The set $|\mathcal X|$ consists of field-valued objects modulo the equivalence identifying two objects when they become isomorphic over a common field extension. A point is of finite type if it has a representative $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\mathcal X$ locally of finite type. An algebraic stack means a stack in groupoids with representable diagonal and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; stack, 2-fibre product and representability by algebraic spaces use [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Properties of representable morphisms are tested after scheme base change on etale scheme charts.

proof.text: Apply the finite-type-point residual-substack lemma to $x$. Obtain a reduced locally Noetherian algebraic stack $\mathcal Z$ and a representable fully faithful locally finite type map $i:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$, with $|\mathcal Z|$ a singleton mapping to $x$. This application requires no finiteness condition on the base scheme.

The relative diagonal of $\mathcal Z$ is unramified. Indeed, a map $T\to\mathcal Z\times_S\mathcal Z$ specifies two objects $u,v\in\mathcal Z(T)$. Its base change of the diagonal is the sheaf of isomorphisms from $u$ to $v$. Full faithfulness of $i$ on every $T$-scheme identifies this sheaf, over $T$, with the sheaf of isomorphisms from $i(u)$ to $i(v)$. The identification sends an isomorphism to its image under $i$; full faithfulness gives its unique inverse, and pullback compatibility follows because $i$ is a functor over the base. Thus it is an isomorphism of sheaves over $T$. The latter sheaf is exactly the base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/S}$ by $(i(u),i(v))$, so it is an algebraic space unramified over $T$ by the assumed meaning of unramified relative diagonal. Thus every scheme test of $\Delta_{\mathcal Z/S}$ is unramified. This is the test-scheme form of the cartesian diagonal square for a fully faithful map.

proof.text: The stack $\mathcal Z$ now has all hypotheses of the singleton-stack field-cover lemma: it is algebraic, reduced, locally Noetherian, and has one point, and its relative diagonal is unramified by step 2. Choose the resulting field $k$ and representable surjective etale morphism $z:U=\operatorname{Spec}k\to\mathcal Z$. In particular its unique point maps to the unique point of $|\mathcal Z|$.

source.place: Tag 06N0 (lemma-DM-residual-gerbe), as applied in the first construction paragraph of Tag 06N3.

proof.text: Put $a=i\circ z:U\to\mathcal X$. It represents $x$, since the only point of $\mathcal Z$ maps to $x$. The chartwise calculus says etale maps are smooth, smooth maps are locally of finite presentation, and local finite presentation implies local finite type. Thus $z$ is locally of finite type. The same calculus gives stability under composition for representable locally finite type maps, so $a$ is representable and locally of finite type, as required.

source.place: Tag 06N3 (theorem-DM), first paragraph: composition after the etale field cover; spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03XG and 06LT.

proof.text: For any $S$-scheme $T$, a $T$-point of $U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ consists of maps $p,q:T\to U$ and an isomorphism $i(zp)\simeq i(zq)$. Full faithfulness of $i$ gives a unique isomorphism $zp\simeq zq$ in $\mathcal Z(T)$. The same correspondence on arrows is inverse to applying $i$ and commutes with pullback in $T$. It therefore identifies $U\times_{\mathcal X}U$ with $U\times_{\mathcal Z}U$, preserving both maps to $U$. Both fibre products are algebraic spaces, by the representable diagonals of $\mathcal X$ and $\mathcal Z$. The inverse correspondence just constructed therefore gives an isomorphism of algebraic spaces over $U\times_S U$. Each projection $U\times_{\mathcal Z}U\to U$ is a base change of the etale map $z$. The chartwise base-change calculus makes both projections etale. Under the displayed identification they are exactly the two projections asserted in the item. No separability or perfectness assumption on the chosen field has entered the argument.
